_notes:
Adafruit NeoKey 1x4 (product 4980): seesaw firmware on a SAMD09 (hardware ID 0x55) at 0x30, the default (A0, A1 jumpers give 0x31-0x33, not claimed: a seesaw detection writes two bytes, which other chips there would take as a register and data). Seesaw registers are a module base and a function. A read straight after the request returns 0xFF, so each read follows a 5 ms pause
Detection: STATUS_VERSION (0x00 0x02), 5 ms, 4 bytes: the top 16 bits are the Adafruit product number, 4980 (0x1374), the rest a date code
Init: STATUS_SWRST (0x00 0x7F = 0xFF), 20 ms; the four key pins 4-7 (mask 0x000000F0) inputs with pull-ups: GPIO DIRCLR_BULK (0x01 0x03), PULLENSET (0x01 0x0B), BULK_SET (0x01 0x05)
Poll (100 ms): GPIO BULK (0x01 0x04), 5 ms, 4 bytes big-endian; a key is pressed when its pin reads 0, so key1-key4 are bits 4-7 of the last byte, inverted. The 4 NeoPixels (pin 3) aren't driven
Source: pins and registers from Adafruit's seesaw library (Adafruit_NeoKey_1x4); the version and timings checked on the bench

rsao.note: bench (Axiom018, 2026-11-08): the lone 0x99 returns 0xFF; the key pins' pull-ups and the GPIO reads after it unchanged
